introduction: Today the Church commemorates all the faithful departed. We pray for all who have died, especially our own loved ones, that they may be purified and come to the light of God's presence. Ezekiel hears God promise to open the graves of his people and put his Spirit in them. Peter speaks of a living hope through the Resurrection. Jesus raises the only son of a widow at Nain. Let us pray for the dead with hope.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God has given us a living hope through the Resurrection of Jesus Christ. With faith, let us pray for all the faithful departed.
intentions: For all the faithful departed, especially our families and friends: that God may bring them into his light and peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have died without anyone to pray for them: that the Lord may welcome them in his mercy. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who mourn: that Jesus may say to them, as to the widow of Nain, Do not weep. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the dying: that they may meet the Lord with faith and hope. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may live in the hope of the resurrection and one day be reunited with those we love. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God of the living and the dead, your Son had compassion on the widow and raised her son to life. Grant to all the faithful departed a share in his Resurrection, and comfort those who mourn. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Do not weep
reflection.body:
On this day, the Church remembers all who have died and prays for them. We believe that our prayers, and above all the Mass, can help those who are being purified before they see God face to face. In praying for the dead, we express our faith that love is stronger than death.

Ezekiel is led into a valley full of dry bones, a picture of a people who have lost all hope. God tells him to prophesy, and promises: "Behold, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves, my people." And: "I will put my Spirit in you, and you will live." What is impossible for us is possible for God.

Peter gives thanks for this hope: God "caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, to an incorruptible and undefiled inheritance that doesn't fade away." Even in grief, he says, believers can "rejoice greatly with joy that is unspeakable."

In the Gospel, Jesus arrives at the town of Nain as a funeral procession comes out. A young man has died, "the only born son of his mother, and she was a widow." She has lost everything. Luke tells us, "When the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said to her," Do not cry. He touches the coffin and says, "Young man, I tell you, arise!" And "he gave him to his mother."

Jesus does not raise every dead person in this life. But this sign shows us his heart toward all who mourn, and his power over death. One day he will speak that word to all the faithful departed.

Today, pray by name for those you have lost. Visit a grave, light a candle, or ask for a Mass to be offered. And let Jesus speak to your grief: do not weep.
